title: The Secret Detention
premise: Coral Thackeray, seventeen and de facto parent to her younger siblings, finds coded instructions hidden in her late grandmother's recipe box — directions that lead to sealed school board records from a decades-old scandal. Following them pulls her into a secret society of students who have guarded the truth for generations, bound by an oath of silence that once destroyed her grandmother's friendship and reputation. As Coral uncovers evidence that the board buried a toxic contamination cover-up still affecting the school's water, she must choose between the loyalty the society demands and the truth her family deserves — especially when her own mother's name appears in the buried files. In the climax, Coral breaks the oath at a public board meeting, exposing the documents at great personal cost; the resolution sees the scandal acknowledged, the society dissolved into something honest, and Coral finally allowed to be a teenager instead of a caretaker.
about_author: V. M. Eastwick is the pen name of a former night-shift nurse who wrote this debut on break-room napkins and lunch-hour drafts. Eastwick grew up in a rust-belt town where everyone knew what the school board preferred forgotten, and writes stories about kids who keep secrets they never agreed to carry.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Between packing lunches and covering her mom's night shift, Coral sorts her late grandmother's recipe box and finds a card with measurements that spell out coordinates and a date. The emotional beat: curiosity cracking through exhaustion — the first thing in years that belongs only to her.

chapters.title: The Careful Life
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A portrait of the Thackeray household: twelve-year-old Dex's skipped homework, little Junie's nightmares, bills taped to the fridge. Coral realizes the recipe card's date matches a school board meeting three weeks away. Beat: the weight of being needed versus wanting more.

chapters.title: Room B Under the Gym
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, brief shift to Dex. Following the card's directions after hours, Coral finds a hidden door beneath the gym bleachers and is caught by Priya Nair, a senior who recognizes 'a Seeker's summons.' Beat: fear flipping into belonging she didn't know she was starving for.

chapters.title: The Order of the Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya explains the society: founded by Coral's grandmother and four friends in 1979 to guard evidence of a board cover-up, passed down student to student under an oath of silence. Beat: awe curdling as Coral learns her grandmother was expelled for it.

chapters.title: What Grandma Buried
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the society's archive room, Coral finds her grandmother's confiscated notebook: chemical test results showing solvent contamination in the school's groundwater — never remediated, just retested and buried. Beat: grief braided with fury.

chapters.title: Oathbound
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The current five members vote on whether Coral may stay; the oath requires absolute secrecy, even from family. Coral swallows the lie she'll have to tell Dex and Junie. Beat: the first taste of how loyalty can feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Water Marks
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Dex notices rust stains and a strange taste at school, starts his own quiet investigation, and nearly stumbles onto the archive door. Coral covers, lying to his face. Beat: guilt — she's becoming the adults who hid things.

chapters.title: The Fifth Chair
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Member Marcus reveals the society's rule-keeper, Mr. Aldous Vane, is the son of the 1979 board chairman — and has been quietly steering the society toward permanent silence for years. Beat: dawning suspicion inside the sanctuary.

chapters.title: Mom's Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In a 1990s follow-up file, Coral finds her mother listed as a teenage witness who recanted after 'family circumstances were addressed' — their eviction, their poverty. Beat: betrayal and heartbreak; the secret already broke her family once.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral confronts her mother before a night shift; Mom admits she was paid off and threatened, and begs Coral to let it stay buried. Beat: love against duty — both women protecting each other in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Vane privately offers Coral a scholarship fund 'arrangement' if she helps seal the archive permanently when the building is demolished next month. Beat: temptation wearing a helpful face; the deadline becomes real.

chapters.title: Junie Knows
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Eight-year-old Junie has been drawing the recipe-box symbols for weeks; she followed Coral one night. Instead of anger, Coral tells her a half-truth — and gains an unexpected ally. Beat: tenderness; secrets shared become lighter.

chapters.title: The Retest That Never Was
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The society obtains a lab contact who confirms recent samples exceed safety limits; the demolition would bury the evidence forever. One member defects to Vane's side. Beat: the group fractures along the loyalty-versus-truth fault line.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Someone reports the Thackerays to child services over 'unsupervised minors'; a caseworker visit nearly unravels everything. Coral suspects Vane. Beat: terror that the system will take her siblings for her defiance.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Card
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Decoding the final recipe card, Coral finds a letter: her grandmother meant for a grandchild to finish this, apologizing for the burden but trusting 'the careful ones see clearest.' Beat: blessing and inheritance; resolve hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The society votes: hand everything to Vane or go public. It ties, then Marcus flips after learning Vane falsified his college recommendation. They plan disclosure for the final board meeting before demolition. Beat: fragile unity forged from broken trust.

chapters.title: Caseworker's Mercy
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The caseworker returns unannounced during the plan's riskiest errand; Coral chooses honesty about their situation, and the woman quietly advocates for the family instead. Beat: vulnerability rewarded — asking for help isn't failure.

chapters.title: Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. On the eve of the meeting, Vane changes the archive locks and files a police report about 'stolen records.' The originals are trapped; only Coral's grandmother's duplicate cards point to a second cache. Beat: despair, then the scramble.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Racing the demolition crew's early arrival, Coral, Priya, Dex, and Junie retrieve the duplicate evidence from the condemned natatorium's filter room — where the contamination began. Beat: breathless climax of the heist; siblings as a team at last.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the open session, Coral breaks the society's oath publicly, reads her grandmother's letter, and presents the test results as Vane tries to gavel her down — until a board member's own grown daughter stands to corroborate. Beat: the climax; truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Fallout: state investigation launched, Vane resigns, the demolition halted pending remediation. The society formally dissolves its oath, becoming an open student archive club. Beat: bittersweet reckoning — some friendships don't survive the light.

chapters.title: A New Recipe
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later: clean water testing begins, Mom takes a day-shift job, and Coral adds her own card to the box — not a secret, but a record, signed by all three siblings. Beat: belonging redefined; care freely given instead of duty silently carried.
